Combined state after the host account inventory page lands on top of the earlier approved role editor state that included the inventory card: the role editor descriptor host_account_inventory moves from an embedded card of the assets page to its own page entry (placement page, no placement entries); every other value equals that earlier approved state, which this entry supersedes for these scenarios.

The inventory read response gains next_identity, the login identity a scan started now would use: its mode and, for the default account, the account name. For an asset without a dedicated bastion account it reads default_account with the default account name; every other field keeps its value.

Reading an asset's host account inventory now uses the same visibility decision as reading the asset itself: a connection grant on the asset, or the asset inside the caller's management scope. The asset-wide view permission that every signed-in person holds does not count. These subjects cannot read this asset's details, so they now get the same not-found response for its inventory instead of its results; for them this supersedes the earlier approved body expectation for this inventory endpoint.

The request audit record of the inventory read follows its response: for subjects who cannot see the asset it records a failure with status 404 instead of a success with status 200; every other column is unchanged.
